watchlist.landing: Marblehead — Tucker's Wharf & State Street (Philip Clark) Landing
watchlist.reason: Real town-owned landings in the flagship premium catchment (median HH ≈1.5× the metro's $115,863; no rail in town; deep-water harbor, 3,000+ moorings) — but the only standing right is a 30-min public tie-up, which is not a schedule-grade berth. North Shore Line extension held pending a negotiated recurring berth with the harbormaster; do not render as a station.
watchlist.note_internal: THE gating item for the flagship North Shore Line extension. Priority dock-track workstream: negotiated recurring commercial berth at Tucker's/State St. Never surface berth-negotiation status in rendered copy.

watchlist.landing: Swampscott — Albert J. Williams Town Pier / Fish House pier
watchlist.reason: Real town pier + float system, affluent catchment (median HH $134,386), but documented shoaling — harbor 'too shallow for many commercial boats at low tide'; tide-window operation or dredging required before any promotion. Do not render as a station.

watchlist.landing: Cohasset Harbor — public docks + Cohasset Harbor Marina
watchlist.reason: Among the richest waterfront towns in MA (median HH $199,306), but the harbor has a 7-ft approach, a tight rocky entrance, and is tide-constrained for a 30–45 ft commercial vessel. Likely permanent answer: road-feed to the Hingham interchange. Do not render as a station.

watchlist.landing: Gloucester — Solomon Jacobs Public Pier + Cape Ann Marina
watchlist.reason: Real landings, but grant terms may restrict commercial use of Solomon Jacobs; Cape Ann Marina is up the Annisquam, not the inner harbor; and at ~28 nm from Boston the run falls outside the 20–45 min sweet spot. Growth-phase at best. Do not render as a station.

watchlist.landing: Chelsea — Marina at Admiral's Hill (Island End River)
watchlist.reason: The only real landing in Chelsea (private marina; seasonal slips + transient dockage), but Island End River channel depth/approach is unknown, and Chelsea's own public-dock study found no ferry-ready public dock in the city. Do not render as a station.

no_landing.reason: No passenger dock exists; the only funded Mystic crossing here is a planned bicycle/pedestrian bridge to Everett (target ≈2029). Any Assembly Row landing is net-new Chapter 91 permitting work. Paper only.

Boston Harbor Now's dock report states there is no existing or proposed ferry-service dock in Chelsea; the Mary O'Malley State Park landing slip is documented as decayed. Only the private Admiral's Hill marina exists (watchlist).

no_landing.area: Kendall Square / Cambridge / entire Charles River basin
no_landing.reason: The Charles is impounded behind the Charles River Dam at North Station — harbor access only via the Gridley Locks (~30,000 boat lockings/yr, each transit a full lock cycle) plus an MBTA commuter-rail drawbridge whose openings are restricted during peak rail hours (M–F ~6:15–9:10 AM). NOT reachable from the harbor at commuter frequency; the entire basin (Kendall, MIT, Esplanade, CambridgeSide) is off-network. A Charles in-basin electric ferry concept exists but is a proposal, not a service.

incumbent_respect.rule: MBTA/Massport run a proven harbor ferry system — 1,498,200 riders in 2025 (~2,700/weekday), the highest on-time performance and farebox recovery of any MBTA mode, and a year-round F10 inner-harbor loop added in 2026. Navier renders ONLY as a premium employer-sponsored tier on top of that system plus marina-grade stations the MBTA does not serve (Salem, year-round Marina Bay, Beverly). NO displacement framing anywhere: copy never claims to replace, beat, out-compete, or fix the MBTA; incumbents are respected proof points and potential partners (WETA-style).
usable_public_proof_points: MBTA ferry: 1,498,200 riders in 2025; highest OTP and farebox recovery of any MBTA mode
F1 Hingham direct: 18 weekday round trips; F2H: 19; F4 Charlestown: 39 trips on a 10-min crossing
Salem Ferry sells commuter-rate rush-hour tickets — a private operator already monetizes a North Shore commute

inner_harbor_no_wake_honesty.rule: Boston Inner Harbor is a no-wake zone beginning at the NW corner of Logan Airport — a hydrofoil is foil-borne only OUTSIDE the inner harbor (President Roads / Nantasket Roads / Broad Sound); every inner-harbor leg runs at displacement speed like everyone else. Segments flagged speed_constrained:true must render water_min as 'indicative — subject to Boston Harbor speed rules' — never a bare number. ALL published trip times must model the displacement leg. NO 'foiling into downtown' or foil-speed-to-the-dock claims anywhere in copy. A zero-wake hydrofoil gets no automatic exemption; do not soften this in copy.
constrained_zones: Inner-harbor no-wake zone from the NW corner of Logan Airport (minimum wake; secondary sources cite 5 kt within 300 ft of shore / 10 kt within 1,000 ft)
Entire Mystic/Chelsea reaches, including the full Encore corridor (plus the Alford Street Route 99 drawbridge)
inner_harbor_no_wake_honesty.note: BOS-6 (Inner Harbor Shuttle) and BOS-9 (Riverside Shuttle) are all-no-wake lines with zero hydrofoil advantage — sell on guaranteed seats, frequency, and experience, never speed or time.

sea_state_honesty.rule: North Shore and outer legs (Salem, Beverly, Lynn, Scituate) cross Broad Sound / open Massachusetts Bay — semi-open Atlantic. The incumbent Salem Ferry cancels for rough seas multiple days at a time (documented multi-day cancellations, Oct 2025). NO all-weather or every-day service claims for these legs. Copy states a published weather-cancellation policy and notes that commuter-rail fallback exists at Salem and Beverly.
sea_state_honesty.note_internal: Winter ops: year-round operation is proven — MBTA runs F1, F2H, F4, and F10 all winter; the harbor core does not ice-lock in normal winters; Mystic upper-reach icing unknown. Internal only — do not render winter/ice discussion.

logan_held_decision.rule: The Logan Water Transportation Dock is verified PASS (public, Massport, multi-operator) but Boston↔Logan is a HELD corridor in Navier partner/operator materials — NO Logan stop, line, or map marker in this hub under any circumstances. The decision_ledger array is internal-only and never renders. Water paths may pass Logan's frontage geometrically; no marker or label appears there. Include-on-microsite is a Jaideep decision.

gates.no_invented_landings: Every stop maps to the exact named landing in BOSTON-NODE-INVENTORY.md. Any stop that cannot be ID-matched to a real BP goes to the bp_gap ledger with reason and renders only from inventory-named coordinates — never guess.
gates.times_indicative: ALL times marked indicative until Atlas geometry seals them; inner-harbor displacement legs must be modeled in every published time.
gates.loi_framing: Non-binding letter of intent — a seat-block interest signal, not a purchase.
gates.no_dock_negotiation_language: No copy about dock deals, berth negotiations, Chapter 91/DEP permitting, DCR/Massport terms, or landing agreements — internal only.
gates.launch_timing: Service launch not before end-2027. All network rendering is coverage narrative, not a service promise; seat economics still gate corridor launch (60–80 committed seats).

copy.hero: Your dock becomes a station on a connected water network. Boston already proves the harbor commute — the MBTA ferry carried nearly 1.5 million riders last year and now runs a year-round inner-harbor loop. Navier adds a premium employer-sponsored tier on top: 20-seat electric hydrofoils linking Salem, Hingham, Hull, Quincy Marina Bay, downtown, and the Seaport — including year-round marina-grade stations the public system doesn't serve today.

sections.why_boston: Boston has the 4th-worst traffic congestion in the US (~$1,400 lost per driver per year), and I-93 south of downtown is the 2nd-most-congested road in the country. Meanwhile the harbor commute is already proven: the MBTA ferry is the system's best-performing mode, Hingham and Hull commuters ride 18–19 round trips a day, and when the Sumner Tunnel closed, the state itself pointed the North Shore to the water. Every launch station is a working ferry landing or marina today — no new construction on day one.
sections.how_it_works: Employers commit seat blocks on a corridor. When a corridor reaches 60–80 committed seats, it launches. Seats are guaranteed, quiet, working commutes on zero-emission electric hydrofoils.
sections.network: Three launch lines — the North Shore Line (Salem · Long Wharf · Seaport/Fan Pier), the South Shore Express (Hingham · Hull · Rowes Wharf · Fan Pier), and the year-round Quincy Line (Marina Bay · Long Wharf) — with Long Wharf as the primary interchange and Fan Pier and Rowes Wharf as transfer points. Phase 2 and 3 stations render as planned, not promised.
sections.alongside_the_mbta: The MBTA and Massport run one of the best public ferry systems in America — we're building alongside it, not against it. Navier adds guaranteed employer seats where the public boats are full or don't go: a Seaport leg for South Shore riders, year-round service at Marina Bay, and a Salem station the network has never had.
sections.north_shore_weather: Salem and Beverly legs cross open water, so we publish a weather-cancellation policy up front — and on rough-sea days, commuter rail from Salem and Beverly is the fallback. We'd rather tell you that now than surprise you in November.
sections.inner_harbor_speed: Inside the inner harbor, every vessel — including ours — observes no-wake speeds. Our hydrofoils earn their time on the open-water legs; every travel time shown is indicative until routes are finalized with harbor authorities.
sections.timing: Targeting first service no earlier than end-2027. The map is a coverage plan, not a schedule.
sections.loi_ask: Register interest with a non-binding letter of intent. It costs nothing and reserves nothing — it tells us which corridors to launch first.
